reasoning: The aliasing hazard is real but the location and reachability in the finding are off. AtomKokkos::add_custom() (atom_kokkos.cpp:450-526) always backs the custom arrays with Kokkos allocations -- e.g. IVEC: `memoryKK->grow_kokkos(k_ivector, ivector, nivector, nmax, "atom:ivector")`, so atom->ivector[i] is a row pointer INTO a contiguous Kokkos view. The base FixPropertyAtom::grow_arrays() (src/fix_property_atom.cpp) then does `memory->grow(atom->ivector[index[nv]], nmax, "atom:ivector")`, i.e. a realloc() of an interior pointer into a Kokkos allocation -- heap corruption. However the finding's claim that 'nothing forces the /kk variant' is only half true: AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() (atom_kokkos.cpp:167-168) does contain `if (!ifix->kokkosable) error->all(FLERR, "KOKKOS package requires a Kokkos-enabled version of fix property/atom");`. That check simply never runs unless at least one property/atom/kk fix already exists, because update_property_atom() is only ever called from FixPropertyAtomKokkos::post_constructor() and ~FixPropertyAtomKokkos(). Reachability is also narrower than stated: AtomKokkos::new_avec() (atom_kokkos.cpp:610) already refuses a non-kokkosable atom_style, so a KOKKOS run must have suffix_enable on with suffix 'kk', and Modify::add_fix() applies that suffix to internal add_fix() calls too (modify.cpp:858-864). The base FixPropertyAtom is therefore only instantiated if the script turns the suffix off (`suffix off`) or names the style explicitly. Real defect, but a guard gap rather than a routine failure.
fix: Make the guard unconditional: move the `if (!ifix->kokkosable) error->all(FLERR, "KOKKOS package requires a Kokkos-enabled version of fix property/atom")` loop out of AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() into a place that always runs -- e.g. iterate modify->get_fix_by_style("^property/atom") in AtomKokkos::init() (atom_kokkos.cpp:155) and error there, or perform the same check at the top of AtomKokkos::add_custom().

The sharing is real and matches the finding exactly. kf_bfly_generic (kissfft_kokkos.h:377-413) takes the plan state by const reference and does `typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_DATA_1d_um d_scratch = st.d_scratch;`, then writes `d_scratch(q1).re/.im` and reads `C_MUL(t,d_scratch,q,...)`. st.d_scratch is a single per-plan allocation made once in kiss_fft_alloc_kokkos (line 520: `st.d_scratch = typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_DATA_1d("kissfft:scratch",p_max);`). kiss_fft_functor (fft3d_kokkos.cpp:177-193) holds `kiss_fft_state_kokkos<DeviceType> st;` BY VALUE, but a Kokkos::View member copies as a reference-counted handle to the same memory, so every one of the `Kokkos::parallel_for(total/length,f)` work items (fft3d_kokkos.cpp:261 and the mid/slow equivalents) writes the same p_max elements. The CPU original is per-call: src/KSPACE/kissfft.h:340 `auto *scratch = (FFT_DATA *) KISS_FFT_TMP_ALLOC(sizeof(FFT_DATA) * p);` ... :362 `KISS_FFT_TMP_FREE(scratch);`. kf_bfly_generic is only reached from kf_work's `default:` case (kissfft_kokkos.h:453) when the radix p is not 2/3/4/5. I adjust the severity down to low because it is unreachable today, and I verified the gate the finding only asserted: FFT3dKokkos is instantiated nowhere but PPPMKokkos (pppm_kokkos.cpp:879,884), and PPPM::set_grid_global boosts EVERY dimension -- including a user-supplied `kspace_modify mesh` grid, since the boost at KSPACE/pppm.cpp:1168-1172 sits outside the `if (!gridflag)` block -- until PPPM::factorable() accepts it, with factors[] = {2,3,5} only (pppm.cpp:92-96, 1198-1210). So p is always in {2,3,4,5} and the generic butterfly is never entered. It is a trap for the next user of FFT3dKokkos, and a real race on any threaded host backend (Kokkos::OpenMP) if it ever is.
fix: Give each concurrent 1d FFT its own scratch. Either allocate st.d_scratch with p_max*(total/length) elements and have kf_bfly_generic index a subview based on the functor's work item (thread the FFT index down through kiss_fft_kokkos/kf_work alongside Fout_count), or switch the parallel_for to a TeamPolicy and take the buffer from Kokkos team scratch memory sized p_max. As an interim guard, error out in kiss_fft_alloc_kokkos when kf_factor returns a p_max > 5 rather than silently racing.
